Major duties include but are not limited to: Medical Gas Systems Maintains and repairs piped medical gas systems including oxygen, nitrous oxide, and vacuum systems. Responds to alarms, traces pressure drops, tests outlets with flow meters, and isolates faulty zones.

Adjusts regulator pressures, calibrates alarm thresholds, and verifies flow rates at outlets. Coordinates with third-party vendors for annual certification and responds to deficiencies. Liquid Systems Maintains and repairs domestic and process water systems, including potable water, RO/DI systems, and sanitary waste systems.

Follows emergency water supply procedures. Installs, repairs, and maintains plumbing fixtures including water closets, tubs, showers, and sinks. Addresses plumbing issues such as sewer main backups, water leaks, and fixture failures. Lubricates pump bearings, flushes mixing valves, and monitors pump operation.

Inspects pressure gauges, valves, and piping for leaks, corrosion, or damage using flashlights, mirrors, and thermometers. Replaces leaking pipe sections, failed pumps, and PRVs using appropriate joining methods, pipe wrenches, soldering tools, and thread sealant.

Tests repaired lines for pressure integrity, verifies pump operation, and performs backflow preventer testing. Cleans sewer mains semi-annually using high-pressure jetters or mechanical augers. Therapy pool Maintains and repairs therapy pool systems to ensure safe water quality and mechanical reliability.

Cleans filters, lubricates pump bearings, and inspects chemical feed lines. Performs daily water chemistry testing for bromine, pH, and alkalinity; inspects motors, valves, and adjustable pool floor. Verifies pump and lift operation and maintains inspection logs for compliance with health and safety standards.

Irrigation Systems Installs, maintains and repairs below ground watering systems to include sprinklers and drip lines to ensure efficient water distribution for lawns and landscapes. Performs system startups, seasonable adjustments, troubleshooting malfunctions and programs controllers.

Fire Suppression Systems Maintains and repairs fire suppression systems in accordance with NFPA 25 and VA safety standards. Replaces sprinkler heads, valves, flow switches, and pipe sections using pipe wrenches and sealant. Adjusts pump pressure switches and calibrates alarm thresholds.

Performs weekly/monthly fire pump tests, annual hydrant flushing, and alarm/flow switch verification. Documents all testing and maintenance activities; coordinates with contractors for annual NFPA inspections and 5-year internal pipe inspections. General Maintenance Coordinates with contractors for large-scale projects.

Ensures compliance with building codes and safety standards. Performs other duties as assigned.

Work Schedule: Monday-Friday, 7:30am-4:00pm Position Description Title/PD#: Plumber/PD618-60860A Critical Skills Incentive (CSI): Not Authorized Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not authorized The VA Midwest Health Care Network advocates for a Whole Health System of care in each of the Medical Centers.

This is an approach to healthcare that empowers and equips people to take charge of their health and well-being and live their lives to the fullest. As an employee operating in a Whole Health System of care, you will operate in a model with three core elements, seeking to create a personalized health plan for each Veteran.

This is done in the context of healing relationships and healing environments and a connection back to the Veteran's community. This aligns with the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Mission Statement to Honor America's Veterans by providing exceptional health care that improves their health and well-being.
To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 09/08/2026. EXPERIENCE: A specific length of training and experience is not required, but you must show evidence of training or experience of sufficient scope and quality of your ability to do the work of this position.

Evidence which demonstrates you possess the knowledge, skills, and ability to perform the duties of this position must be supported by detailed descriptions of such on your resume. Applicants will be rated in accordance with the OPM Federal Wage System Qualification Standards. Preferred Experience: 1. General plumbing experience 2.

Able to estimate materials needed for job 3. Able to solder copper pipe. 4. Troubleshoot and repair domestic hot and cold water systems 5. Interpret blueprints 6. Experience working with fire suppression systems 7. Experience working on medical gas systems 8.

Experience working on compressed building air systems SCREEN-OUT ELEMENT: Your qualifications will first be evaluated against the prescribed screen out element, which usually appears as question 1 in the on-line questionnaire.

Those applicants who appear to possess at least the minimal acceptable qualification requirement are considered for further rating; those who do not are rated ineligible and are eliminated.

The potential eligibles are then rated against the remainder of the Job Elements: Equipment Assembly, Installation, Repair Interpret Instructions, Specifications (includes blueprint reading) Measurement and Layout Technical Practices Troubleshooting Use and Maintain Tools and Equipment Without more than normal supervision Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religions; spiritual; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Note: A full year of work is considered to be 35-40 hours of work per week.

Part-time experience will be credited on the basis of time actually spent in appropriate activities. Applicants wishing to receive credit for such experience must indicate clearly the nature of their duties and responsibilities in each position and the number of hours a week spent in such employment.

Physical Requirements: Lifts and carries materials and equipment weighing up to 50 pounds, occasionally weighing up to 100 pounds. Bends, kneels, crouches, and stands for extended periods. Uses hand and power tools requiring coordination and manual dexterity. Works in confined spaces and performs tasks that involve considerable physical effort.

You will be asked to participate in a pre-employment examination or evaluation as part of the pre-employment process for this position. Questions about physical demands or environmental factors may be addressed at the time of evaluation or examination.

Working Conditions: Works in mechanical rooms, patient care areas, and outdoors, exposed to varying temperatures and weather conditions. Subject to noise, fumes, and vibrations from tools and equipment.

Works in potentially hazardous environments, requiring adherence to safety protocols and the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves, safety glasses, and hearing protection. Occasionally encounters biological and chemical hazards and follows stringent hygiene and safety practices.

· Independently installs, modifies, repairs, and maintains a variety of new and existing utility, supply, and disposal systems and equipment such as medical gas systems, sewage, water, oil, and gas distribution systems, and water closets, tubs, backflow prevention devices/assemblies, fire suppression systems, and showers. - Plans and accomplishes work from initial layout to final assembly which involves interpreting and applying building plans, specifications, blueprints, sketches, and other plumbing, medical gas, fire suppression and backflow prevention guides/codes, and using shop mathematics. - Troubleshoots/tests various medical gas systems, fire suppression, plumbing systems and equipment including backflow prevention devices such as reduced pressure principle devices, double check devices, atmospheric vacuum breakers, and other cross connection devices. - Uses and maintains tools such as tapes, rules, plumb bobs, hand and power pipe threaders, cutters, pipe wrenches, angle drills, hacksaws and power saws, power sewer cleaning equipment, various gas detectors and meters. Medical gas outlet analyzer, backflow pressure differential gage, and other specialized equipment/tools. - Utilizes safety practices and procedures following established safety rules and regulations and maintains a safe and clean work environment. Uses and assures proper fit of required safety equipment and clothing.
In order to qualify, you must meet the quality level of experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards Handbook X-118C. QUALIFICATIONS: Applicants will be rated in accordance with the OPM Qualification Standard Handbook X-118C for the WG-4200 PLUMBING AND PIPELIFTING GROUP.

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most blue-collar positions, you must meet any screen-out element listed, and show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on the quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. The screen out element for this position is the ability to do the work of a WG-4206 PLUMBER without more than normal supervision.

JOB ELEMENTS: Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of equipment assembly, installation, operation, and repair, to include routing, placement, slant, slope, and fall of systems. 2.

Knowledge of technical practices in order to plan, lay out, install, modify, troubleshoot, and repair various systems and equipment. 3. Knowledge of safety regulations, procedures, and practices. 4.

Skill in installing, modifying, and repairing new and existing utility, supply, and disposal systems and equipment without more than normal supervision 5. Skill and ability in using shop mathematics, measurement, and lay out such as angles, arcs, and circles. 6.

Skill in using and maintaining tools and equipment such as rules, levels, plumb bobs, dividers, various gauges and meters, various drain cleaning devices, hydrostatic pumps, and torches. 7. Skill in troubleshooting difficult or hard-to-detect leaks and operating problems.

Physical Effort: The plumber makes repairs and installations from ladder, scaffolding, and platforms, and where the parts of systems worked on are in hard-to-reach places. This requires the employee to stand, stoop, bend, kneel, climb, and work in tiring and uncomfortable positions.

The plumber frequently lifts, carries, and sets up parts and equipment that weigh up to 40 pounds unassisted and over 40 pounds with assistance. Working Conditions: required to make repairs and installations outside in bad weather. The plumber will be required to work under extreme stressful conditions in surgery rooms, critical care units, etc.

The plumber will be expected to respond quickly to emergency situations, alleviate condition by quick decisive action. The plumber will be required to makes repairs in areas where bad smelling fumes and odor are present.

The plumber has occasional exposure to the possibility of broken bones and frequent exposure to the possibility of scrapes, burns, and infections. Will be required to wear safety equipment, such as safety shoes, glasses, gloves, and hard hats and other personal protective equipment.

PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week.

VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

· Relevant Experience: Prior experience as a plumber in large environments such as cruise ships, offshore platforms, or other high-passenger vessels is highly preferred. Experience with complex plumbing systems onboard or in related industries will be considered valuable.

dasteam ag gehört zu den national führenden Stellenvermittlungen mit insgesamt 27 Standorte in der Schweiz und im Fürstentum Liechtenstein. Als Sanitärinstallateur\*in EFZ/EBA bist du verantwortlich für die Installation und Reparatur moderner Sanitäranlagen in anspruchsvollen Neubauten sowie für die Renovierung bestehender Anlagen. Du arbeitest in einem dynamischen Team, in dem der Austausch von Ideen und Erfahrungen geschätzt wird.

Du bist in der Lage, komplexe Sanitärsysteme zu verstehen und diese effizient zu installieren. Zudem sorgst du für die Einhaltung von Sicherheitsstandards und Qualitätsvorgaben.

Deine Arbeit trägt dazu bei, dass unsere Kunden mit den neuesten Technologien und Lösungen im Sanitärbereich versorgt werden. Wir suchen jemanden, der nicht nur handwerkliches Geschick mitbringt, sondern auch die Fähigkeit im Team zu arbeiten und Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

As a PLUMBER, WG-4206-09, you will install and repair interior pipe systems and plumbing fixtures and appurtenances and maintains pipe systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment. Installs, tests, troubleshoots and repairs pipe systems designed to conduct flow of hot and cold water interior sewage.

Installs and maintains pipe systems located above, under and on the ground; in, on and between walls, floors and ceilings; and, at mobile and stationary missile facilities. Installs plumbing fixtures, appliances, potable and non-potable water, interior sewage, and air and gas systems.

Connects pipe sections using fittings and soldering, brazing, or packing oakum and lead will or hot head. PHYSICAL EFFORT: Performs duties which require standing, stooping, bending, kneeling, climbing and working in tiring and uncomfortable positions. Frequently lifts, carries, and sets up tools, parts and equipment that weigh up to 50 pounds.

Makes repairs and installations from ladders, scaffolding and platforms, and where parts of systems worked on are in hard-to-reach places. WORKING CONDITIONS: Work is performed both inside and outside. Inside work is usually in buildings, adequately heated, lighted and ventilated. Noise from saws, hammers and power tools is frequent.

Dust, mud, dirt and snow are prevalent on construction sites. Has occasional exposure to the possibility of broken bones, cuts. electrical Shocks. and respiratory ailments. Has frequent exposure to the possibility of Scrapes, burns, and infections.

Exposure to repeated, prolonged or concentrated amounts of refrigerant gases may cause toxic effects to eyes. skin, and internal organs.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: WG09 Must have at least 18 months of experience or training using plumb tools such as bobs, mercury gauges, dividers, closet augers, hydrostatic pumps, and lead pots.

Experience installing and operating new and existing utility, supply and disposal systems and equipment such as sewage, water, oil, and gas distribution systems, and water closets, tubs, fire sprinkler systems, and showers. Experience working from building plans, blueprints, and sketches.
